page: Microsoft Azure E64s_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the ESv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, delivering 64 virtual CPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on external Premium Storage options.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing and memory capabilities. The server achieves top-tier results in multi-core CPU performance, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and software compilation tasks. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is highly efficient, with read speeds of 296.85 GB/sec and write speeds of 136.92 GB/sec. However, single-core performance and text processing benchmarks fall within the average range. Large-scale LLM text generation is a notable bottleneck, with the 70B model achieving only 2.73 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E64s_v5 offers high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it suitable for memory-intensive enterprise workloads without the overhead of GPU hardware. The primary tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage, requiring architectural reliance on network-attached storage. This configuration is highly suited for relational database operations, in-memory caching, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing pipelines.
